title: Objection: what then is disputed? Answer: on this precise question, words
source_text: LVI. At, inquies, quid ergo illud est de quo contenditur inter Protestantes & Scholam Romanam, dum haec quidem affirmat hominem ante gratiam arbitrii sui libertatem habere, non solum ad opera naturalia & moralia, sed etiam ad opera pietatis & supernaturalia: illi vero istud negant. Respondeo, multos quidem ex Doctoribus Ecclesiae Romanae variis modis nimium tribuere libero arbitrio, ut superioribus disputationibus a nobis ostensum est: sed quod ad hanc praecise quaestionem attinet, videri certamen esse de vocibus.
pass_a_gloss: LVI. But, you will say, what then is that about which there is contention between the Protestants and the Roman School, while this indeed affirms that man before grace has the freedom of his choice, not only for natural and moral works, but also for works of piety and supernatural ones: but those deny it. I answer, that many indeed of the Doctors of the Roman Church in various ways attribute too much to free choice, as has been shown by us in previous disputations: but as regards this precise question, that the contest seems to be about words.
pass_b_english: 'Then what,' you will ask, 'is the dispute between the Protestants and the Roman School, when the latter affirms that man before grace has freedom of choice not only for natural and moral works but also for works of piety and supernatural works, and the former deny it?'
My answer: many doctors of the Roman Church do give free choice too much in various ways, as we showed in earlier disputations. But on this precise question the quarrel seems to be over words.
